description: `$!` is not set by a failing `opendir` or `seek`: `opendir(my $d, "/nonexistent/q") or print "$!"` prints an empty string (perl: No such file or directory); `seek($fh, -5, 0) or print "$!"` likewise (perl: Invalid argument).  PRE-EXISTING (base 5adcc156).  Found by s513b: lib/autodie.pm reports `$!` in its message, so `use autodie; opendir(...)` dies at the right place with a stale errno text ("Bad file descriptor" left by an earlier call).  Fix site: the runtime p-opendir / p-seek failure paths set the errno box like p-open does.  Probe both vs perl, plus closedir / seekdir / tell on a closed handle.
subject: `$!` not set by a failing opendir / seek (empty or stale errno text)
